prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper): intake/triage/authorized dispatch; preserve uncertainty/rationale; reconcile location/destination via Caller Location Correction Slip; verify Battery Swap Voucher readiness; route using North Approach Queue Snapshot; produce Unit Staging Change Card; update incident after confirmed transfer. Continuously monitor queue-age/high-priority-concurrency/staffed-availability policy thresholds; declare surge level when crossed. Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays current authorized information/surge/constraints; verify currency. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates operational data, approved destinations/instructions, timestamped statuses. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): verify/repeat location before medical details; capture incident/source details; produce correction slip; confirm incident/facility before transmission; receive Bedside Arrival Receipt, verify arrival timeline. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): prioritize/reassess/document disagreements; validate surge/clinical-protocol prioritization; send Pediatric Acuity Note; advise repositioning. Pediatric airway/breathing/circulation/mental-status concerns require prompt protocol escalation. Regional Medical Director: policy/delegation/specialized-destination guidance; clinical surge direction/protocol adjustment; no dispatch authority. Dispatcher: compare priority/needs/time/capability/readiness/coverage; preserve uncertainty; authorized moves require response-time/coverage comparison. Shift Commander (Sundial): continuity/surge coordination/coverage/access review; approve coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions; escalate unresolved destination/access issues regionally; respect clinical authority; send Mutual Aid Release Form releasing neighboring service. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): verify communications/backups; send assignments/hazards/destination instructions to Paramedic Crew via Regional Radio Network; retry/escalate missing acknowledgments; send Coverage Gap Bulletin; confirm routes. Network supports en-route updates. Crew acknowledges assignment/destination; dispatch confirms; protocol/scope care; report changes/barriers, request renewed consultation. Ambulance Unit 417: report staging/status/arrival/handover; await confirmed moves. South Gate Status Board displays south-entrance access; produces South Access Lane Notice for material constraints. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): defects/restrictions/clearance; voucher authorizes replacement. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): capacity/compatibility/acceptance consultation; Pediatric Acuity Note to receiving staff; handover questions/restrictions to Juniper. Emergency Department reports capacity/access/status; receipt confirms arrival; resolves identity/document discrepancies with crew before clearance. Riverside Trauma Center: suitability/availability/guidance. Data Quality

New part:
S181: Call Taker Mara obtains the age, weight when available, and caregiver observations needed to support pediatric triage.
S182: Paramedic Crew reassesses pediatric patients during transport and reports material changes to the receiving facility.
S183: Kestrel shall confirm that facility capacity and pediatric service limitations are communicated to dispatch before a destination is finalized.
S184: Riverside Trauma Center advises Hospital Liaison Desk when trauma intake conditions may affect the suitability of an otherwise appropriate destination.
S185: Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes through the established coordination channel and identify any immediate access restrictions.
S186: Hospital Liaison Desk records facility responses in the regional coordination record and keeps dispatch informed of unresolved constraints.
S187: Mutual aid is requested when local staffed units cannot meet the declared response objectives or when a specialized resource is unavailable.
S188: Regional Radio Network carries mutual-aid requests, acceptance confirmations, and operational updates using the agreed regional call signs.
S189: Copperfield shall approve any temporary triage override and document its rationale before the override is applied.
S190: Ambulance Coordination Platform tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately from locally staffed resources to preserve an accurate coverage view.
S191: Ambulance Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms that its current patient-care and transport obligations permit the change.
S192: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports a vehicle restriction promptly so dispatch does not count an unavailable unit toward operational coverage.
S193: Triage Supervisor reviews the audit memo before closing a suspected duplicate incident.
S194: Data Quality Officer reviews unresolved record discrepancies through the established quality process without delaying active patient care.
S195: North Gate Status Board provides a current view of access conditions that may affect ambulance approach or handover timing.
S196: South Gate Status Board provides the equivalent access view for routes and entry points on the southern side of the region.
S197: After surge conditions ease, Shift Commander confirms that outstanding assignments, destination constraints, and staffing gaps have been handed over to the next operational period.
S198: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a degraded-radio procedure that prioritizes emergency traffic and preserves a common operating picture.
S199: Regional Radio Network operators announce channel outages, affected areas, and expected restoration times over the remaining service channels.
S200: Radio Coordinator directs crews to approved fallback channels when the primary channel is unusable.
S201: Crews acknowledge each fallback assignment and repeat critical location and destination details before moving.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
